sources.findings: Clinical symptoms do not establish confirmation. Investigations depend on illness day: CBC/Hct, NS1 and liver tests in first five days; antibody pathway from day six. Home eligibility depends on assessments, not reassuring symptoms alone. Adult paracetamol ceiling 3 g/day is not a full prescription. Avoid NSAIDs/steroids and retain return precautions. Null history/examination cannot establish absence of risk.

Figure 8: after one month of amlodipine 5 mg daily with target unmet, standard step 2 adds losartan 50 mg daily. Footnotes require adherence review and creatinine/potassium checks before and several weeks after losartan. Women who may become pregnant must not receive losartan/ACEi/ARB; separate step 2 increases amlodipine to 10 mg daily. Current pregnancy has a distinct specialist-referral instruction. Monthly review after medicine initiation/change; treatment should not be universally delayed for unavailable initial tests.

Outbreak changes suspected-case definition. Severe criteria take precedence; some dehydration requires no danger signs and at least two listed signs, with Plan B and admission. ORS 75 mL/kg over four hours, hourly reassessment and additional ongoing losses. Antibiotics are conditional, including severe dehydration, pregnancy or elderly status; discharge requires all listed conditions.

Probable case requires clinical plus epidemiological criteria; confirmation requires laboratory evidence. Dengue may overlap/co-infect; manage suspected chikungunya with dengue precautions until excluded. A negative NS1 alone is insufficient in the still-febrile case. PCR within five days; source antibody timing retained. No acute physiotherapy; source-specific medication ceilings must not be blended. Admission triggers include instability, oliguria, altered sensorium, bleeding, persistent disabling symptoms after treatment and high-risk groups; joint pain alone does not establish every trigger.
